newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen up 1 to 2 cts, pork bellies up limit.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen up 1 to 2 cts, pork bellies up limit.

text.p: CME hog futures were called 1.00 to up the 2.00-cent-per-lb limit with the greatest gains in the October and forward contracts after USDA on Friday reported a smaller-than-expected breeding herd, analysts said.

Pork bellies were called sharply higher to up the 3.00-cent limit in reaction to the report and to higher cash belly prices Friday. Cash bellies, 12- to 14-lbs, were quoted Friday at $88.00 per cwt by USDA, up $3.00.
In hogs, higher cash hog prices at Midwest markets plus higher cash pork prices Friday was seen supportive to nearby hog futures.
Plus, some analysts said a U.S. hog herd of 102 percent, as reported by USDA Friday, was slightly smaller than many analysts expected, which should encourage buying in nearby contracts.
